scope_note: Reference examples are illustrative CE-RISE workflows. The assistant may generalize reusable patterns from them, but must not treat their product examples, payloads, auth choices, ports, or local-only settings as defaults for every adopter.

examples.title: Digital Passport System Local Demonstrator
examples.example_role: Local-only deterministic reference workflow showing how existing CE-RISE Digital Passport services, storage, model registry entries, payloads, and smoke checks can be exercised together.
concrete_example_elements: Docker Compose stack with HEX Core Service, JSON DB storage service, PostgreSQL, and optional RE Indicators Calculation Service
fictional product records used as demonstration payloads
local no-auth configuration for deterministic development runs
record creation, persistence, read-back, and validation checks

generalizable_patterns.title: Declare scope and actor roles before running a workflow
generalizable_patterns.generalized_action: Replace the demonstrator's fictional product context with the adopter's actual product, material, asset, process, or lifecycle scope and value-chain roles.
not_assumptions: Do not assume the demonstrator's fictional products are relevant to the adopter.
Do not assume the demonstrator's data fields are complete for another scope.

generalizable_patterns.title: Select CE-RISE services and storage deliberately
generalizable_patterns.generalized_action: Use the demonstrator to understand service interactions, then choose the CE-RISE services and storage pattern needed for the adopter's target workflow.
not_assumptions: Do not assume the optional RE indicators service is always required.
Do not assume local PostgreSQL-backed storage is the production storage decision.

generalizable_patterns.title: Adapt the model registry catalog
generalizable_patterns.generalized_action: Use the demonstrator's registry catalog pattern to identify the model artifact URLs needed by the adopter's passport scope.
not_assumptions: Do not assume the demonstrator's catalog entries cover every adopter scope.
Do not vendor model artifacts when the existing CE-RISE publication workflow should be used.

generalizable_patterns.title: Prepare representative valid and invalid payloads
generalizable_patterns.generalized_action: Translate the demonstrator's valid/invalid payload pattern into adopter-specific payload examples with expected validation outcomes.
not_assumptions: Do not reuse fictional payload data as adopter evidence.
Do not treat a passing sample payload as compliance certification.

generalizable_patterns.title: Exercise the intended record lifecycle
generalizable_patterns.generalized_action: Use the demonstrator's create, persist, query, and read-back sequence as a pattern for the adopter's intended passport record lifecycle.
not_assumptions: Do not assume the demonstrator's no-auth local session handling applies outside local development.
Do not assume every workflow needs record creation in the first planning stage.

generalizable_patterns.title: Turn demo checks into operational checks
generalizable_patterns.generalized_action: Generalize the demonstrator's scripted checks into environment-appropriate smoke, readiness, validation, and rollback checks.
not_assumptions: Do not use local-only no-auth checks as production acceptance criteria.
Do not treat demonstration success as deployment readiness without environment-specific checks.

adaptation_questions: What product, material, asset, process, or lifecycle scope replaces the demonstrator's fictional examples?
Which value-chain actors provide, validate, consume, or enrich the passport information?
Which CE-RISE model artifacts are relevant to the declared scope?
Which payloads should be valid, invalid, incomplete, or edge-case examples for this adopter?
Which services are required now, and which optional services can be deferred?
What authentication, storage, and deployment decisions differ between local development and production?
reuse_boundaries: The demonstrator is a reference example, not the target architecture for every adopter.
Local no-auth configuration is for deterministic development only.
Fictional payload content is not adopter evidence.
Deployment handover should use the CE-RISE GitOps template and component documentation.
